The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `28f2cc1f737a2f1900429c761135023f4045fdba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/push-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts + docs/adr/0012-notification-platform.md (§6 amended domestic-vendor bullet, §6.1), packages/spec/src/api/push-relay.zod.ts (`PushRelayDeliverySchema.vendor`), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.vendor`), packages/services/service-push/src/push-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-push/src/push-service.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/push-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/user-device.object.ts (`sys_user_device`)

Inputs: card #29960 (body; comments 6611521127, 6665182964, 6666461990, 6666548945, 6667839156), PR #30631 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `dc5181124`), and the head's check-runs. The PR body and the dev reports were read as claims; every judgment below is against the tree. `origin/main` has moved 12 commits past the merge-base; `git diff dc5181124 origin/main` on the six PR paths, ADR-0012, `push-relay.zod.ts`, `protocol.zod.ts`, `service-push` and the messaging push files is empty, so the head's reading is `main`'s reading.

Gate verdicts, read at 2026-11-05T20:09Z after every run had completed: 69 check-runs on the head, 59 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 0 in progress. The ten required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (carries `check:docs`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`), `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI` all `success`; `Lint UI` `skipped` (no `ui/` path in the diff). The skipped ten are path-filtered or opt-in jobs (`Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Temporal Conformance`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Schedule gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `18.x upgrade harness`, `Lint UI`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **No shape, `.describe()`, default or export moves — right.** Every `+`/`-` line in the two `hits` hunks is a ` * ` docblock line. At the head, `PushVendorSchema` is still `z.enum(['apns', 'fcm'])` with its `.describe()` byte-identical to `main`, `UserDeviceSchema.vendor` is still `PushVendorSchema.describe('Push vendor the token belongs to: …')`, and no export, `strictObject` guidance map, alias or default in either file moved. The accept set of `PushServiceConfigSchema`, `PushDirectTransportConfigSchema`, `PushRelayTransportConfigSchema` and `UserDeviceSchema` is unchanged; `check:api-surface` and `check:authorable-surface` are green on the head inside `TypeScript Type Check`.
- **The published surface does move, in text only — right, and the diff carries its one derived artifact.** The module docblock of `push-config.zod.ts` is the source of `content/docs/references/system/push-config.mdx` (`build-docs.ts`), and the regenerated page's hunk is the "Out of scope here" paragraph and nothing else; `check:docs` is green. The two docblocks also ship in `dist/**/*.d.ts` (`packages/spec/package.json` `types` entries; the tsup DTS pass), so the published declarations' documentation text changes — the reason ② is a patch, not "no changeset".
- **Consumers of `PushVendorSchema` are untouched and need no change — right.** Its consumers on `main` are `UserDeviceSchema.vendor` (push-device.zod.ts:58), `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.vendor` (protocol.zod.ts:3711, "apns or fcm; absent, derived from platform"), `PushRelayDeliverySchema.vendor` (push-relay.zod.ts:93, "apns or fcm"), the `PushVendor` type in `service-push` (the `transports` record keyed by vendor in `push-plugin.ts` and `push-service.ts`), and `sys_user_device.vendor` (`Field.select` of `apns` / `fcm`, user-device.object.ts:77). None carries the retired "alternate channel" reading, so none is owed an edit; the test-file header is the only other carrier and it moves in the same PR (lane seat's accept).
- **Nothing is left behind.** A grep of the head tree for `alternate channel`, `separate channel`, `plug in as`, `channel plugin` and `plugin-notification-push` across `packages/spec/src`, `content/docs`, `packages/services`, `skills` and `docs` (ADR-0012 excluded) finds only unrelated hits: ADR-0013 / ADR-0022 (messaging channel plugins, a different subject), `email-service.ts` / `sms-service.ts` (transports that plug in, a different subject), a `design/` note that predates the amendment, and the new test header, which carries the amended reading.
- **The Docs Drift Check comment (6666462165)** reported the two `.zod.ts` files as yielding no anchor. That is the advisory backstop saying the hand re-read is owed; this record is that re-read (the `push-config.mdx` reference page is in the diff; `push-service.mdx` was re-read, see ④).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **patch** — right. The diff publishes documentation text in the declarations and the generated reference page; no runtime, no schema shape, no accept-set, no export and no default moves, so nothing above patch is owed and nothing below it would carry the TSDoc change into `CHANGELOG.md`. `Clause-②: no` — right: no narrowing, no capability taken from a consumer, no refusal made real. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: no authorable key, guidance map or alias on `PushServiceConfigSchema` or its blocks moves (`check:authorable-surface` green). The changeset body states exactly what the diff does ("Comment text only … `PushVendorSchema` stays `apns | fcm`"), cites the ADR by section and carries no tracker number or model identifier. `check-changeset-no-major` and the changeset gates are inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`push-device.zod.ts` :12 left unchanged** ("the stored device shape of the push device registry (ADR-0012 §6, narrowed to what core ships)") — **answered: right to leave.** §6 is still "Push channel — device lifecycle", the device registry and its invalidation loop; its amended text names `UserDeviceSchema` as "the shipped device shape … narrowed to `apns` | `fcm` and `ios` | `android` | `web`". The citation is about the registry shape, not the retired plugin reading. The same holds for the other §6 citations the PR leaves in place and I read: `push-device.test.ts` :3, `protocol.zod.ts` (the registration header), `push-plugin.ts` ("ADR-0012 §4, §6"), `user-device.object.ts` ("ADR-0012 §6, §11"). The dispatch's assumption that :12 carried the plugin reading was wrong; the dev's deviation is the correct call.
- **The merge of `main` (af8fca1b6)** — **answered: accepted.** It is a merge, not a rebase, of a branch the dev alone pushed; the net diff against merge-base `dc5181124` is the six files and nothing from `main`; no path in scope moved on `main` since. The head's check-runs are on the merged tree, and the queue leg re-runs the required set against `main` at landing.
- **The widened surface (`push-service.mdx`)** — **answered: in order.** The claim amendment 6666548945 records the widening on the card before the round-1 push, it is the same defect family on a hand-written page the docblocks do not feed, the path is not governed, and the sentence lands in this PR; it is the lane seat's accept at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not reviewed here. Read as an observation in ④.
- **`open_questions`** in both dev reports: `[]` — nothing to answer or escalate.
- **The round-0 deviation "did not merge `origin/main` before opening the PR"** is superseded by the round-1 merge; the round-1 deviation "the docs sentence cites no ADR" is a page-voice choice on a file outside the contract face — noted, not a defect.
- **Lane seat's remainder** (test-file header, regenerated reference page, `push-service.mdx`, changeset): ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` as a standalone PR of those files. The test header moves no assertion (comment lines only); the reference page is what `build-docs.ts` emits (`check:docs` green); the changeset is judged in ②.

### ④ Design judgment

Every new sentence in the two `hits` files was tried against ADR-0012 §6 (the amended domestic-vendor bullet) and §6.1 on `main`, and against the code on `main` that routes on `vendor`.

**`push-config.zod.ts`, module docblock, "Out of scope here" paragraph.** "Out of scope here: the domestic Android vendors (HMS / Honor, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo). ADR-0012 §6.1 has the hosted relay front them in phase 2, as further values of `vendor`, the token type the relay routes on; there is no per-vendor plugin and no per-vendor channel." — **TRUE.** §6.1: "phase 2 adds the domestic vendors (HMS / Honor / Xiaomi / OPPO / vivo) behind the same relay and widens `PushVendorSchema` with them. There is no per-vendor plugin and no per-vendor channel." §6: "In phase 2 the relay fronts HMS / Honor / Xiaomi / OPPO / vivo as well". It describes phase 2, not a served relay; the same docblock's "What is served today" paragraph and the relay block's `[PLANNED — not yet served]` `.describe()` still say the relay is not served (held: `PushServicePlugin.init` throws `PUSH_RELAY_NOT_SERVED_MESSAGE` on any non-direct transport). Complete for its purpose, which is to say what this file does not configure.

**`push-config.zod.ts`, `PushVendorSchema` docblock.** "Push vendors core delivers through: `apns` (Apple) and `fcm` (Firebase)." (unchanged) — **TRUE**: `service-push` builds `ApnsPushTransport` and `FcmPushTransport` from the direct block and nothing else. "Closed on purpose. `vendor` is the token type the hosted relay routes on (ADR-0012 §6.1): phase 1 routes these two, and phase 2 adds the domestic Android vendors (HMS / Honor, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo) behind the same relay, with no per-vendor plugin and no per-vendor channel." — **TRUE** against §6.1's third bullet, which it restates in the ADR's own tense ("Phase 1 routes `apns` and `fcm`; phase 2 adds …"); "phase 1 routes" and "phase 2 adds" are parallel plan statements, and no sentence says the relay delivers today. "So a new value here is a spec change made together with its transport: the relay's routing for that vendor." — **TRUE and load-bearing**: §6 cites this docblock for exactly that phrase ("its docblock says a new value is a spec change made together with its transport"), and the PR keeps it verbatim and names the transport as the relay's routing, matching "`PushVendorSchema` widens to those values in the same change that routes them". The `.describe()` is unchanged and still true.

**`push-device.zod.ts`, `UserDeviceSchema` docblock, "Narrowed from" paragraph.** "Narrowed from the ADR-0012 §6 sketch: `vendor` is the core pair (`apns` | `fcm`; it is the token type the hosted relay routes on, and the domestic Android vendors join it in phase 2 behind the same relay, ADR-0012 §6.1) and `platform` is the registration's own three (`ios` | `android` | `web`)." — **TRUE.** The §6 sketch enumerates seven vendors and five platforms; the shipped shape narrows to the pair and the three (`PUSH_DEVICE_PLATFORMS`, shared with `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema`), as §6's amendment records. "join it in phase 2 behind the same relay" is §6.1. Nothing in the paragraph says the relay is served; :12 above it still cites §6 for the registry, correctly (③).

**Sentences the PR leaves in place, re-read for truth now:** the module docblock's "it refuses the relay transport, not yet served" (held by `push-plugin.ts`), "What is served today" (held), the direct-transport paragraph citing §4 (held), and `push-device.zod.ts`'s "`@objectstack/service-push` holds only the vendor transports and never touches the table" (held by `user-device.object.ts`'s header and `push-plugin.ts`). None is now false.

**Observation on the lane seat's `push-service.mdx` sentence** (not a driver of the verdict): "Only `apns` and `fcm` ship today. The other Android vendors (HMS / Honor, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo) are planned for a later phase behind the hosted relay (below), as further values of `vendor`, the token type the relay routes on, and not as plugins or channels of their own." — true against §6/§6.1, and "(below)" lands on the page's own "The hosted relay: not served yet" section, so the page does not describe the relay as served.

**Findings.** No must-fix. Two should-fix, neither a falsehood:

- **S1 (should-fix, both `hits` files): "the token type the hosted relay routes on" names only the relay.** On `main` the relay is not served and the direct transport is what routes on `vendor` today — `PushService.send` picks `transports[message.vendor]` (`push-service.ts` :92) and the push channel filters the recipient's devices by the vendors the service has transports for (`push-channel.ts` :147). ADR §6 puts it as "so the sender knows where the delivery goes". The standalone `PushVendorSchema` TSDoc (what an IDE hover shows, with no module docblock beside it) therefore gives the relay-only reading. Proposed: "the token type the sender routes on — the direct transport today, the hosted relay (the default) once served (ADR-0012 §6.1)". Carrier: this PR, one clause in each file; the regenerated page follows.
- **S2 (should-fix, both `hits` files, minor): the vendor list's separators.** "HMS / Honor, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo" reads as four vendors with HMS and Honor as one; the ADR's amended lists write "HMS / Honor / Xiaomi / OPPO / vivo" five ways, and its §6 sketch enum has `hms` and no `honor`, so whether Honor is its own token type is left to the phase-2 widening. All five names are present, so nothing is false. Proposed: the ADR's five-way list. Carrier: this PR (punctuation only), together with S1.
